Subject: StarLumen RFP — ask on pricing breakdown and packaging

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the KV-cache examples. We received the internal RFP and procurement wants a clearer view of how your pricing maps to our usage profile. High level asks:

- A seat vs consumption comparison for a 6-month pilot and annual rollout (we expect bursty peaks up to 300 rps for a subset of endpoints)
- What credits or uplift you can offer for a 90-day pilot (we typically ask for pilot credits to offset migration risk)
- Packaging options: hosted API vs dedicated pool vs a hybrid (we may want a dedicated pool for PII workloads)
- Any limits/exceptions on caching/kv-credit accounting we should be aware of

I've attached the RFP and the security questionnaire — procurement will need those answered before a PO. Can you send a short commercial sketch today so we can align internally?

Subject: RE: StarLumen RFP — ask on pricing breakdown and packaging

Hi Natalie — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Below is a concise sketch that maps to the scenarios you outlined. Happy to jump on a quick call this afternoon if useful.

Summary (short):
- Option A — Hosted (consumption-first): $0.0009 / token (generation) with standard embedding unit at $0.004; good for low-touch pilots, no infra commitment; ideal if you want immediate access and easy scale.
- Option B — Dedicated pool (reserved capacity): monthly commit for a 4x GPU pool (T4-equivalent) at $65k/mo with predictable throughput, per-token runtime discount (≈35% lower than hosted) and an SLA. Better for predictable high-throughput routes and PII isolation.
- Option C — Hybrid (hosted + dedicated routes): routed by workload — training/eval and non-PII on hosted, PII and high-volume inference on dedicated; blended pricing based on usage mix.

Commercial levers we can offer for StarLumen pilot:
- 90-day pilot credit: $30k credit to apply against hosted usage;
- Migration uplift: one-time onboarding credit of $12k for dedicated pool setup (if you choose Option B);
- KV/Prefix caching allowance: first 500k cached tokens per month free for pilot; beyond that we can discuss a tiered charge.

Operational notes / limits:
- KV cache credits apply per model variant; large multi-variant deployments may need adjusted cache budgets.
- Dedicated pool pricing assumes model family compatibility; significant quantization or custom kernel work may impact setup timeline (we'll flag during technical kickoff).

Next steps:
1) If this aligns, Jordan can prepare a formal 90-day pilot SOW and DocuSign.
2) We can schedule a 30-minute technical kickoff with Connor to validate model compatibility and needed SLAs.

I attached a brief one-pager (inline below) and can convert to a formal quote if procurement wants numbers in a line-item table.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen

Forwarding with suggested commercial specifics so procurement has a table to review.

— Suggested line-item sketch (for procurement table) —
1) 90-day pilot (hosted consumption): up to 10M tokens + embedding units, apply $30k credit => net cost estimate: $18k (illustrative).
2) Dedicated pool (optional onboarding add-on): $65k/mo commit; onboarding credit of $12k applied to first invoice.
3) Hybrid routing fee: No extra charge for routing; billing split by route usage.
4) KV cache allowance: first 500k cached tokens/month waived for first 3 months. Excess billed at $0.0001 / cached token unit.

Commercial flex: We can reallocate part of the pilot credit to onboarding credit (e.g., $20k pilot + $10k onboarding) if procurement prefers to see direct setup offset.

I'll open a HubSpot deal and drop a DocuSign link for the pilot SOW today.
